question: do I have to declare a major right away or can I stay undecided for a bit
answer:
You can stay undeclared for a while, but not indefinitely. Ramapo says undergraduate students pursuing a bachelor’s degree must declare in their sophomore year before completing 64 credits [7]; matriculated students must declare by 64 credits toward graduation [10]. After completing 64 credits, you are considered a junior and must have declared [2]. For an undeclared student with at least 48 but fewer than 64 credits who is enrolled for a subsequent term, the college gives notice to declare before registering for more than 64 credits; a registration hold prevents registration if you try to register for 64 or more credits without a major. Submit the online Major/Minor Declaration form to the Registrar; upon receipt, it removes the hold and you can register [10].

If you intend to graduate in four years, aim to declare during sophomore year. Most majors take at least two years to complete and usually have foundation classes you can take in your first year; some sequential science majors should be started right away. Recommended Graduation Plans can help plan your first semester [3].

Undeclared students are advised through the Ramapo Exploration Program (REP) by academic advisors in the Center for Student Success [6]. Contact the Center for Student Success for advisement: (201) 684-7441 or success@ramapo.edu [5]. As an undeclared student, select “No Changes” if you do not wish to declare now [8].
